name: PlanProtocol
summary: Puts the standard procedure at the knowledge level, so that a plan is an instance of something configured rather than a shape someone remembers to repeat.

roles.name: Protocol
roles.summary: The procedure as a type object: an ordered set of steps that plans are drawn from. It is the knowledge level of a plan, so changing how the work is meant to be done is configuration and not a new plan per case.

roles.name: ProtocolReference
roles.summary: One step of a protocol, and the protocol that step refers to. That indirection is what lets protocols compose — a step is itself a whole procedure — without a protocol containing copies of another.

roles.name: ProtocolDependency
roles.summary: That one step must follow another. Both are steps of the same protocol and the graph is acyclic, exactly as in a plan; the difference is that this is stated once for every plan the protocol yields.

roles.name: Steps
roles.summary: The references making up the protocol, in order. The components a protocol reaches are derived from its steps' referred protocols rather than listed a second time.
